web.title: European Space Agency - Wikipedia
web.description: The European Space Agency (ESA; pronounced /ˈiːsə/ EE-sə) is a 23-member international organisation devoted to space exploration. It has its headquarters in Paris and a staff of around 3,000 people globally as of 2025. ESA was founded in 1975 in the context of European integration.
snippets: At the ministerial council of 2025, ESA member states widened the agency's mandate to include defence. The resolution reads: "ESA's intergovernmental framework provides the credentials and tools for developing space technologies and systems [...] for security and defence and to implement corresponding activities." After World War II, many European scientists left Western Europe to work with the United States.

The Western European nations decided to have two agencies: one concerned with developing a launch system, ELDO (European Launcher Development Organisation), of which Renzo Carrobio di Carrobio became the first Secretary General from 1964 to 1971, and the other the precursor of the European Space Agency, ESRO (European Space Research Organisation), led by Pierre Auger.

The agency continued its contribution to the International Space Station (ISS) programme with European astronauts joining assembly flights as well as long-term missions to the station. In 2008, ESA added its laboratory module Columbus to ISS and started launching the ATV cargo spacecraft.

This resulted in the first successful orbital launch from Western European soil performed on 5 September 2026 by Isar Aerospace's Spectrum rocket from Andøya Spaceport. The agency's facilities date back to ESRO and are deliberately distributed among various countries and areas.

snippets: The largest single announcement was a €760 million (approximately $844 million) contract that the European Space Agency formally awarded to The Exploration Company on Wednesday, covering the first demonstration of the company's Nyx cargo capsule to the International Space Station and options for two additional service missions.

Among the evening session's announcements on Tuesday, one had direct implications for what European human spaceflight looks like by 2027. Macron, alongside Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis and Aschbacher, confirmed that ESA astronaut Thomas Pesquet — who has accumulated 396 days in orbit across two prior ISS expeditions — will serve as Commander of the commercial Vast-PAM-6 mission. Subject to approval by the Multilateral Crew Operations Panel — the five-agency consensus body that governs all ISS crew assignments — Pesquet would become the first non-American in history to command a US-operated spacecraft.

IRIS² — the Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite — is the European Union's planned sovereign satellite communications constellation, currently under a €10.6 billion (approximately $12 billion) 12-year contract with the SpaceRISE consortium of SES, Eutelsat, and Hispasat. It will eventually comprise more than 350 satellites in low and medium Earth orbit, providing secure connectivity to European government agencies, military forces, and commercial users without reliance on infrastructure operating under non-European legal jurisdictions.

web.title: The European Space Agency headquarters in Paris opens its doors ...
web.description: The ESA headquarters in Paris opens 19-20 September 2026 for free. Talks, an astronaut meet, and an ESA Council simulation are all on the agenda.
snippets: Imagine stepping inside a place where the decisions are made that send satellites into orbit and shape Europe’s planetary exploration ambitions. This weekend, on 19 and 20 September 2026, the European Space Agency headquarters in Paris opens its doors to the general public for the second edition of its Open Days, as part of the European Heritage Days.

Visitors can attend talks led by space industry specialists and meet an ESA astronaut in person, a tangible opportunity to put a human face to missions unfolding hundreds of kilometres above our heads. ... The ESA Council simulation deserves special mention. It offers a window into how member states make the major decisions that steer the Agency, so this is not just a technical deep-dive, but also a look at the governance behind European space cooperation.

The ESA brings something genuinely new to the 2026 edition. While most heritage sites invite visitors to look back into the past, the European Space Agency headquarters in Paris turns the gaze firmly towards the future, towards planetary missions and the technologies shaping Europe’s presence in space.
Located in the 15th arrondissement of Paris since 1976 and fully renovated in 2023, the European Space Agency headquarters in Paris is a strategic site that is normally off-limits to the public.

snippets: Jakob Steinschaden, co-written by newsrooms.ai11. September 2026, 10:15 · The Exploration Company. © TEC · Set Trending Topics as a preferred source on Google. The European Space Agency has just signed a service contract with The Exploration Company (TEC) at the International Space Summit in Paris, the largest transportation contract ESA has ever awarded to a European space company.

That pushes the European model toward commercially delivered services with public agencies acting as anchor customers, much as NASA has done in the United States for years. “This is more than a contract award: it reflects a shift in how we build space technology in Europe,” said Hélène Huby, CEO and founder of The Exploration Company.

The plan covers a first Nyx demonstration flight to the ISS plus two additional cargo missions, either to the ISS or to a future commercial space station. The award marks phase two of a programme ESA member states launched back in 2022 as the Leo Cargo Return Service (LCRS), a competition asking European companies to propose a first step toward a cargo service to and from space stations in low Earth orbit.

Alongside Nyx, TEC is developing Storm, a reusable high-thrust engine running on liquid oxygen and biomethane that is meant to underpin a future European heavy-lift rocket with 40 tonnes of payload capacity. Nyx itself is designed as a reusable, orbit-refuelable capsule able to return up to 3,000 kilograms of cargo to Earth. A demonstrator flight last year ended in partial success, with the capsule lost during splashdown. The timing reflects a broader shift. Demand across the global space sector is rising, driven by connectivity, exploration, defense and new infrastructure in low Earth orbit.
